messages.content: The API isn't working properly. Fix the API integration — and I don't want the provider name showing anywhere in the interface.

Two public, keyless, CORS-enabled JSON APIs now sit behind one client. Each call uses fetch with async/await and an AbortController timeout (9s for current rates, 12s for history), validates the JSON shape before trusting it, and throws a typed FxApiError carrying a user-safe message plus technical detail. On failure it falls back to the second provider, then to a 15-minute localStorage cache, then to a clearly labelled bundled snapshot. src/lib/fx/RateProvider.tsx exposes three states to the UI: loading (skeleton placeholders and a fetching badge), ready (a banner naming the feed and its update date), and error (a dismissible notice with a Retry button and a collapsible technical-details block). The interface names the feed, not the vendor, so no provider name appears anywhere.

Review of the app: (1) the Rate Action Alert either works or goes; (2) the down arrow doesn't move the currency picker; (3) use a key from an env variable and deploy it to Vercel; (4) on the chart the rate should show wherever the date shows; (5) the 24H change reads 0.00% for everything; (6) CSV dates show ### and 90 days only returns 65 rows; (7) is exposing the API acceptable?; (8) the contact info belongs to a different site; (9) remove the marketing copy that isn't true. Plus: remove the Daily Market Email Updates page, remove the Daily currency Market Analysis page, remove footer social links, remove the footer email subscribe, and the contact email must be akhtarabdulmannan@gmail.com.

Worked through the list item by item. The Rate Action Alert was removed entirely rather than patched, along with its route, nav entry, widget tab, call to action, copy, types and data layer — a feature that cannot be verified should not ship. Added full keyboard navigation to the currency picker (arrow keys, Home, End, Enter, Escape, plus proper ARIA roles). Added a custom Recharts tooltip that prints the date and the rate together, so the rate appears wherever the date appears. The 24H change now compares against the previous PUBLISHED business day rather than the same day, which is what made every value read 0.00%. CSV output is now UTF-8 with a byte-order mark, CRLF line endings and quoted fields, so Excel stops rendering dates as ###. Added api/rates.ts as a Vercel serverless function that fetches rates server-side, normalises both provider shapes into one schema, caches for 60 seconds and serves stale for five minutes; FX_API_URL, FX_API_KEY and FX_API_KEY_PARAM are read inside the function, so a key never reaches the browser bundle. Removed the provider name from all user-facing copy. Rewrote contact details around akhtarabdulmannan@gmail.com, removed the false business credentials, and deleted the pages and footer elements that were asked to go.

messages.content: Two separate problems. First, the index.html at the repository root is the Vite source template: its script tag loads /src/main.tsx, which is uncompiled TypeScript, and the leading slash resolves from the root of the drive rather than the folder you extracted, so it looks for C:\src\main.tsx. That file is an input to the build, not a runnable page — it is normal that it shows blank if opened directly. Second, there was a genuine bug in src/main.tsx: a pre-mount redirect ran unconditionally. Under file://, window.location.pathname is the full disk path, so the app rewrote itself to a hash route built from that path and navigated away before React could mount. I fixed it with a protocol guard so the redirect only runs over http and https. I verified the fix by executing the built bundle in jsdom under a Windows-style file path: the app mounts, six children render, about 5,300 characters, zero errors. I also rebuilt the single-file standalone build as a classic inline script so it can be opened by double-click.

WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF INDEX.HTML?

It is the app's shell and the only real HTML document in the project. Its body holds three things: an empty div with id root, a noscript fallback, and a script tag that starts the app. React writes everything else into that empty div at runtime, which is why an empty div means a blank page. The head also owns what React does not: the title, the meta description, theme colour, favicon and font preloads. Because the script tag points at uncompiled .tsx, the file is an input to the build rather than a finished page: after npm run build it is replaced in dist/ with one pointing at the compiled bundle and stylesheet, and the asset paths are rewritten with the repository subpath.

debugging_discussions_summarised.issue: Exchange rate API returning unusable data
debugging_discussions_summarised.diagnosis: Two providers with different payload shapes and no timeout or validation; the UI trusted the response.
debugging_discussions_summarised.resolution: One client with shape validation, AbortController timeouts, typed errors and a fallback chain ending in a labelled offline snapshot.

debugging_discussions_summarised.diagnosis: The comparison used the same day's published rate as both sides, because the feed publishes once per business day.
debugging_discussions_summarised.resolution: Compare against the previous published business day, taken from the history endpoint.

debugging_discussions_summarised.issue: CSV dates rendered as ### in Excel
debugging_discussions_summarised.diagnosis: Plain UTF-8 CSV without a BOM and with LF endings; Excel misread the date column.
debugging_discussions_summarised.resolution: UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF line endings and quoted fields.

debugging_discussions_summarised.issue: Blank page when index.html was opened from disk
debugging_discussions_summarised.diagnosis: Two independent causes: the root index.html is a Vite source template loading uncompiled .tsx, and a pre-mount redirect ran unconditionally so file:// paths navigated away before mount.
debugging_discussions_summarised.resolution: Guarded the redirect with an http/https protocol check; documented that index.html is a build input; added a standalone single-file build for offline viewing.

debugging_discussions_summarised.diagnosis: The Pages site had never been created; the build job succeeded but the publish step had no target.
debugging_discussions_summarised.resolution: Enabled Pages with source GitHub Actions in repository settings, which the assistant could not do because the API returned 403, then the workflow published successfully.

debugging_discussions_summarised.diagnosis: Hand-written counts in the README and report had drifted from the actual source.
debugging_discussions_summarised.resolution: Counted from the source, corrected the figures, and replaced unreproducible test claims with the three commands a reader can run.
